provenance.method: Communication expansion focused on modality rather than deficit labels.

question: I communicate more clearly in writing than in live speech. How can I make that preference usable?
why_it_matters: A person may know exactly what they want to say but lose access to language or processing time in synchronous conversation.
current_understanding: State the functional preference directly: written questions in advance, email or chat for logistics, notes during meetings, or time to send a written follow-up. A communication preference is not evidence of lower understanding or capacity. Services and workplaces may have different constraints, so ask what alternatives are available.
evidence_needed: Service-level evidence on text/email access and outcomes for communication-disabled users.
Research comparing synchronous and asynchronous communication demands across neurodivergent groups.
reopening_conditions: Public accessibility standards strengthen alternative-contact requirements.
Better evidence identifies high-impact communication adaptations.
dissent: Writing is not lower-load for everyone; dyslexia, motor or language difficulties can make speech or AAC preferable.
